hypothesis: All four experiments — including the full baseline — have failed the stability gate, with fell_over consistently in the 1.08–1.49 range during the evaluation window. However, fell_over slopes are consistently negative across runs (the policy IS learning to stabilize, just not fast enough within 3000 iterations). The root cause is that the upright and torso-wobble stability signals are too weak early in training relative to the velocity tracking objectives (weight 2.0 each): the policy preferentially learns to track velocity while tolerating large torso deviations, delaying stable bipedal balance. Doubling upright_reward_weight (1.0 → 2.0) and quadrupling body_ang_vel_reward_weight (-0.05 → -0.2) directly strengthens these early-training stability signals without introducing the competing-objective dynamics that destabilised Experiments 1–3. The upright reward now matches the importance of velocity tracking; the angular velocity penalty creates stronger torso-wobble damping. These two changes target the same failure mode and are semantically coupled (torso uprightness + torso angular stability), so they count as one semantic change. Expected trade-off per rule 6: track_linear_velocity may dip ~5–10% as the policy allocates capacity toward balance — this is acceptable and serves as the diagnostic check.
expected_effects: fell_over_rate drops below 0.5 by iteration ~800–1000 and stays there through the full run — primary success criterion; the stronger upright signal should pull fell_over down faster than the ~-0.001/iter seen in the baseline
fell_over_slope becomes more steeply negative (more negative than -0.001/iter) compared to baseline, indicating the stability signal is taking effect earlier in training

track_linear_velocity reward decreases by ~5–10% (from ~1.25 to ~1.10–1.20) as the policy reallocates capacity to balance — diagnostic check: if it drops more than 15%, the stability weights are too dominant

gait_contact_cv_mean stabilises below 0.4 rather than continuing the monotonic rise to 0.60 seen in all prior runs — more stable gait should produce more regular contact timing as a downstream effect of better balance
body_ang_vel component in the reward should show a more negative mean value (larger penalty being actively incurred and reduced) relative to baseline, confirming the signal is engaged
